This area encompasses the primary population centers in unincorporated parts of the County, such as Guerneville, Forestville, Graton, Sea Ranch and other communities in a non-contiguous fashion, totaling approximately 15,700 in population over approximately 53,000 acres. This work requires a California-licensed Professional Land Surveyor (PLS) to perform record research, boundary analysis, and preparation of final legal and graphic exhibits that comply with the BOE standards.

event_name: RFP Permit Sonoma User Fee Study
description:
The County of Sonoma is pleased to invite you to respond to a Request for Proposal for the Permit Sonoma User Fee Study.

Sonoma County, located at the northern edge of the San Francisco Bay Area, spans approximately 1,768 square miles and has a population of about 480,000 residents. The County delivers a wide range of services both countywide and specifically to the unincorporated areas. The County is soliciting proposals from qualified consulting firms to conduct a comprehensive user fee study for costs of services provided by Permit Sonoma, the County’s consolidated land use and permitting agency. The scope of work includes reviewing all existing fees for services, developing a new cost fee model for the department, and revising fire prevention and hazardous materials fees to achieve full cost recovery. Additionally, the scope includes performing a detailed cost analysis of the Permit Center and reviewing At-Cost project minimum fees and the monthly billing cycle to improve and streamline existing mechanisms used for cost recovery. The resulting recommendations should provide an equitable and sustainable framework that aligns fees with the department’s true cost of service, ensures cost recovery, simplifying the annual fee calculation process.

For questions regarding this specific solicitation, email michelle.arellano@sonomacounty.gov.

All covered employees must be paid at least the increased living wage rate.

description:
The County of Sonoma is pleased to invite you to respond to an RFP to manage and operate Sonoma County Transit. Proposers must be prepared to directly operate this service. No brokers, agents, or subcontracting is permitted. Please carefully review all the attached materials and follow the submission guidelines as requested. Failure to follow the requested guidelines and forms may result in rejection of your proposal.

OPTION PRE-PROPOSAL CONFERENCE: 
A pre-proposal conference will be held as stated on November 12, 2025 (2:00 pm PST) at the Sonoma County Transit Facility, 355 West Robles Avenue, Santa Rosa, CA. The primary purpose of the conference is to acquaint prospective proposers with the transit facility and to allow for a brief inspection of the transit fleet and facilities. Attendance at the conference is not mandatory but is encouraged.

QUESTIONS:
Questions regarding this procurement should be directed to, Transit Systems Manager,  by email to Trish.Pisenti@sonomacounty.gov and Steven.Schmitz@Sonomacounty.gov  .

LIVING WAGE:
The contractor shall comply with any and all federal, state, and local laws – including, but not limited to the County of Sonoma Living Wage Ordinance – affecting the services provided by this contract. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the contractor expressly acknowledges and agrees that this contract is subject to the provisions of Article XXVI of Chapter 2 of the Sonoma County Code, requiring payment of a living wage to covered employees. Noncompliance during the term of the contract will be considered a material breach and may result in termination of the contract or pursuit of other legal or administrative remedies. 

The link to the Living Wage Ordinance is:
 https://sonomacounty.ca.gov/living-wage-self-certificationfor-suppliers  

SUBMISSION:

Refer to Section “Proposal Submittal Instructions and Forms. An incomplete submittal may result in non-consideration, disqualification or rejection of your proposal.
RFP response enclosed in a sealed envelope with the RFP Event: “Event Number 2089 “and RFP Title: “RFP To Manage and Operate Sonoma County Transit” clearly marked on the envelope. Submittals must be received no later than the date and time specified in the schedule above. The official time for submission will be determined by the clock displayed on the lobby’s monitor. 

RFP responses shall be submitted to: 
Event ID: 2089 RFP To Manage and Operate Sonoma County Transit
Attention: Sonoma County Transit Proposal 
Sonoma County Purchasing Division 
400 Aviation Blvd. Ste. 100 
Santa Rosa, CA. 95403

Respondents may view and download bid documents in the County Supplier portal. The link to the Supplier Portal is: https://esupplier.sonomacounty.ca.gov/ . Proposals must be received no later than the date and time listed in the schedule, or as revised by addendum. The RFP schedule is subject to change. If the Schedule is changed, all known recipients of the original bid will be notified via addendum.

Proposals are limited to no more than one hundred (100) pages, exclusive of Price Proposal Forms, certification forms, and supporting documentation such as resumes, training materials, or other exhibits Proposers must submit one (1) electronic copy via the County of Sonoma's Supplier Portal, one (1) hard copy of the proposal , and one (1) copy on a USB flash drive in both Microsoft Word (DOCX) and Adobe Acrobat (PDF) formats.
